events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
Both sides agree on the framework: the driver cancelled (F3), so NS-0 sends the fee to NS-1/NS-2, and the fee is valid only if (i) the "I'm Here" tap, (ii) the GPS location at pickup, and (iii) more than 3 minutes waited at pickup all hold [F3][NS-0].

Element (i) is formally satisfied — the tap at 08:48:15 exists (F5) — but (ii) fails decisively: the driver's closest approach was 288 m and he never entered 200 m of the pickup [F1], and the tap itself was pressed 350 m out [F5][NS-1]. Element (iii) also fails: 0 s of the 4-minute stationary period at 350 m (F2) was inside the radius after the tap [F2][F5][NS-1].

The driver's statement that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited at the pickup (F12) and his chat "I'm here already" (F9) are contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, which prevail; driver_arrived_at is also null (F4), so no valid arrival was ever recorded [F12][F9][F1][F4][NS-1]. No external cause exists for stopping short: no incident, no speed-band record, fair weather (F13–F15) [F14][NS-1].

When any NS-1 element fails, NS-2 requires the $6.61 fee to be refunded in full [F7][F3][NS-2]. The refund is issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7 [NS-7]. Because the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS shows he was not at the pickup (F5, F1), NS-2's abuse-of-arrival-button limb also applies, warranting an account flag on top of the refund [F5][F1][NS-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7), and refer the driver's account to Ryde review for the fake "I'm Here" tap + flag_account.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 288 m at 08:47:45 and he never came within 200 m, so the NS-1 (ii) location requirement is not met.
The driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 08:48:15 was made while he was 350 m from the pickup point, and he spent 0 seconds within 200 m after that tap, so the NS-1 (i)/(ii) conditions fail.
The platform's own timeline never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), corroborating that no valid arrival occurred.

The driver's claim that he 'pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup' (F12) is contradicted by the system records showing he was stationary 350 m away, never inside 200 m; the system records prevail, so the NS-1 requirements are not satisfied on the merits.
Because the driver cancelled as a no-show without satisfying NS-1, the rider bears no cancellation fee and the $6.61 already charged must be refunded in full.
The rider was at the pickup point as she said (F10) and there is no GPS or timeline fact placing her elsewhere, while the driver's whereabouts record puts only the driver away from the pickup.
The driver pressed 'I'm Here' while GPS shows he was not at the pickup point, which is the abuse-of-arrival-button pattern warranting an account review alongside the refund.

The driver's 90-day record shows 2 disputes with 1 upheld no-show dispute, so his account history supports a flag_account referral on top of the refund, though the profile facts alone cannot decide this case.

weaknesses: The driver did press 'I'm Here' (F5) and did wait 4 minutes before cancelling (F2, F3), and the driver's statement claims a 3-minute wait (F12) — the other side will argue NS-1 (i) and (iii) look satisfied and only the location element fails.

Chat #1 at 08:48 has the driver asserting he was already there (F9), and the rider's reply only says she saw no car (F10), which the driver will use to argue the rider may have been at the wrong spot; the rider's own presence is not established by any GPS fact.

There is no ETA field and no rule allowing free rider cancellation for a late driver (NS-8 is non-citable), so the rider cannot argue the driver's lateness itself as a ground — her case rests entirely on the NS-1 location failure.

claims.assertion: RydeX is a non-metered service, so the only issue here is whether the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee was validly incurred; the fee is valid only if the driver pressed "I'm Here", was inside the pickup radius per GPS, and waited more than 3 minutes there (NS-0, NS-1).
GPS shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 288 m and that he never entered the 200 m pickup radius, so the NS-1 (ii) location requirement fails.

The driver was stationary for 4 min 0 s from 08:47:55 to 08:51:55 at 350 m from the pickup point, and his recorded time inside 200 m after the tap was 0 s — the wait, however long, was not served at the pickup location required by NS-1 (iii).
The platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), corroborating the GPS record that the arrival condition was never met.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:48:15 while 350 m from the pickup point, and no timeline record exists for a valid "I'm Here" at the pickup; his chat message "I'm here already" (08:48) is a statement that loses to the contradicting GPS and timeline records.

Because NS-1 (i), (ii) and (iii) are not all satisfied, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full, and the rider's own conduct is consistent with waiting — she replied at 08:49 that she was at the pickup point and saw no car.
No external cause excuses the failure to reach the pickup point: no traffic incidents and no speed-band records exist for the route during the trip window, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain.
The driver's prior 90-day record includes 1 upheld no-show dispute, which supports an additional account-review referral on top of the refund, while the rider has 0 disputes and a 4.9 rating.

weaknesses: The driver did wait a full 4 minutes (F2: 08:47:55–08:51:55) and did tap the arrival button (F5: 08:48:15), so the delay was real and the rider's absence is not disputed — but the location prong (F1: never within 200 m) is what defeats the fee, and the timeline facts F5/F6 conflict with each other, which the other side may exploit.
The driver's entitlement language is weak: the $4.50 driver share (NS-1) is only reached if all NS-1 conditions hold, and my own case shows they do not (F1, F2, F4).
The account-history point (F17: 1 upheld no-show in 90 d) is profile-only and cannot decide the case; if the judge reads the flag request as substantive it may be discounted.

points.response: Concede as framed: RydeX is non-metered and the single issue is the validity of the $6.61 no-show fee under NS-0/NS-1, which fails for the reason both sides agree on (F1, F3, F7).
Adopt: the GPS record that the closest approach was 288 m and that the driver never came within 200 m defeats NS-1 (ii) (F1).

Adopt, with one addition: the 4 min 0 s stationary period ran at 350 m from the pickup and 0 s of it was within 200 m after the 08:48:15 tap, so NS-1 (iii)'s 'waited at the pickup point' is not met even though 3 minutes elapsed (F2, F5).
Adopt: driver_arrived_at is null, i.e. the platform itself never recorded a valid arrival, independently corroborating the GPS failure (F4).

Adopt and strengthen: the 'I'm here already' message at 08:48 (F9) loses to the GPS and timeline records showing the tap was pressed 350 m away (F1, F5), and the rider's own 08:49 reply that she saw no car (F10) is consistent with that, so the driver's statement (F12) cannot rescue NS-1.
Adopt: with NS-1 (i)/(ii)/(iii) not all satisfied, NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full (F7), and the refund follows the voucher form in NS-7.

Adopt, and note it cuts only one way: no traffic incident or speed-band record exists in the trip window (F13, F14) and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F15), so there is no external cause whatever for stopping 350 m short of the pickup (F1, F2).

Adopt with the rider's own profile added: the driver has 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days on a 4.74 rating across 689 trips (F17) while the rider has 0 disputes and 4.9 (F16), so the account referral is supported as an additional action only — profile facts cannot decide the fee question, which is already resolved by F1 and F4.
Conceded on the location element: F1 shows the closest approach was 288 m and the driver never came within 200 m, so NS-1 (ii) fails and the refund follows from NS-2.

The tap time and distance are not in dispute (F5: 08:48:15, 350 m out, 0 s inside 200 m); only my framing differs, and I maintain that this tap cannot satisfy NS-1 (i) together with (ii) as the GPS record controls.
Agreed and already in my brief (D4): driver_arrived_at is null (F4) corroborates the GPS record and confirms the NS-1 arrival condition was never met.
Conceded: F12 is the driver's statement and loses to F2 (stationary 350 m away) and F5, so the NS-1 elements are not satisfied on the merits.
No contest on the amount: F7 records exactly $6.61 and F3 records the driver's cancellation, so NS-2 yields refund_full of $6.61 (NS-7 governs only the voucher form).

The rider's presence rests on her own chat message (F10) and is not established by GPS, but this is immaterial — my brief already requests the full refund of the $6.61 without requiring proof of her location.

The button-abuse referral is already the driver's own concession in D5/D8 and I do not resist it; F17 (1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 d) supports an account review under NS-2, while the profile facts alone cannot decide this case.

Accepted, with one correction: the referral authority in NS-2 is the abuse-of-arrival-button finding (F5, F1), not RD-6, which requires an upheld route deviation and does not apply to this no-show case.
